headline: Parking Permits Required for Backcountry Stays
reservation: Daily entry to the Daniel Boone National Forest is free, but an official parking permit is mandatory for any vehicle remaining in the gorge between 10 PM and 6 AM. These must be purchased at local vendors or forest offices; developed campgrounds require separate reservations via Recreation.gov.

days.title: Arches and the Scenic Byway

stops.name: Nada Tunnel
stops.detail: Drive through the historic 900-foot limestone logging tunnel that serves as the gateway to the gorge.

stops.name: Sky Bridge
stops.detail: Walk the loop trail across a high sandstone span for panoramic views of the Clifty Wilderness.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the scenic loop; roads are narrow with sharp turns.
days.note: Nada Tunnel is one-way; wait for oncoming headlights to clear before entering.

days.title: Ridge Hikes and Hemlock Forests

stops.name: Auxier Ridge Trail
stops.detail: Trek along a narrow rocky spine providing plunging views of the Red River far below.

stops.name: Gray’s Arch
stops.detail: Descend through rhododendron thickets to reach one of the largest and most majestic natural spans in Kentucky.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for forest service roads; gravel conditions vary.
days.note: Tunnel Ridge Road can be closed during high ice or heavy rain events.

days.title: River Valleys and History

stops.name: Gladie Visitor Center
stops.detail: Learn about the geological formation of the arches and the history of the Ironwood people.

stops.name: Chimney Top Rock
stops.detail: Take an accessible walk to a dramatic overlook watching the Red River wind through the forest floor.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for local transit and stopping at overlooks.
days.note: Check official water levels if planning any local river transfers.

intel.title: Trailhead Congestion
intel.text: Lots at Auxier Ridge and Gray’s Arch fill by 10 AM on spring and fall weekends. Have a secondary trail in mind if primary lots are full to avoid parking illegally on vegetation.

intel.title: Deep Gorge Dead Zones
intel.text: Cell service is non-existent in the valley floor near the river and inside Nada Tunnel. Print your maps or use specialized forest GPS units for navigation.

intel.title: Gateway Services
intel.text: The final fuel and grocery stops are located in Slade and Stanton. There are no services once you pass the Nada Tunnel or enter the loop road.

intel.title: Seasonal Activity
intel.text: Autumn is peak climbing season; expect higher pedestrian traffic near crags. Spring brings high water to the river, making some lower crossings difficult.

intel.title: Arch Safety
intel.text: Many arches are located near sheer cliffs without railings. Exercise extreme caution on wet sandstone which can become deceptively slippery.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Blue Grass Airport (LEX) and stop in Stanton for backcountry permits and essential supplies before reaching the Slade gateway.
plan.vehicle: High clearance vehicles are recommended for Forest Service gravel roads, though paved loops are accessible to all; check rental insurance for off-pavement exclusions.
plan.goldenHour: Chimney Top Rock provides a spectacular western view of the gorge, best viewed in the late afternoon depending on the season.
